exposure: elevated fasting blood glucose (FBG) ≥ 5.1 mmol/L at 32-34 gestational weeks
cohort: 1130 singleton pregnancies who had negative GDM screening results in their first and second trimesters.
finding: 6.3% of singleton pregnancies with prior negative GDM screenings developed late-onset GDM when screened at 32-34 GW, and this group had a significantly higher risk of macrosomia and NICU transferring despite standard treatment.
birth_weight: Macrosomia (large birth weight) was an outcome measure.
gest_age: Screening performed at 32-34 gestational weeks; perinatal outcomes of full-term delivery were compared.
